arxiv-1906-07130.title: Explicit and Compact Representations for the One-Sided Green’s Function and the Solution of Linear Difference Equations with Variable Coefficients This paper is an integrated version of an earlier publication with the homonym title. It includes some remarkable theoretical supplements and updated ref
arxiv-1906-07130.creator: A. G. Paraskevopoulos ‡ and M. Karanasos † ‡ University of Piraeus, † Brunel University London
arxiv-1906-07130.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by A. G. Paraskevopoulos ‡ and M. Karanasos † ‡ University of Piraeus, † Brunel University London. Leibniz’ combinatorial formula for determinants is modified to establish a condensed and easily handled compact representation for Hessenbergians, referred to here as Leibnizian representation. Alongside, the elements of a fundamental solution set associated with linear difference equations with variable coefficients of order p p are explicitly represented by p p banded Hessenbergian solutions, built up solely of the variable coefficients.

arxiv-2106-04637.title: Constraining the effect of convective inhibition on the thermal evolution of Uranus and Neptune
arxiv-2106-04637.creator: Steve Markham, Dave Stevenson
arxiv-2106-04637.description: Abstract The internal heat flows of both Uranus and Neptune remain major outstanding problems in planetary science. Uranus’ surprisingly cold effective temperature is inconsistent with adiabatic thermal evolution models, while Neptune’s substantial internal heat flow is twice its received insolation.

arxiv-2404-13748.title: Application of Kalman Filter in Stochastic Differential Equations
arxiv-2404-13748.creator: Wencheng Bao, Shi Feng, Kaiwen Zhang
arxiv-2404-13748.description: Abstract In areas such as finance, engineering, and science, we often face situations that change quickly and unpredictably. These situations are tough to handle and require special tools and methods capable of understanding and predicting what might happen next. Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) are renowned for modeling and analyzing real-world dynamical systems.

arxiv-2501-17704.title: Inferring Implicit Goals Across Differing Task Models
arxiv-2501-17704.creator: Silvia Tulli, Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou, Mohamed Chetouani, Sarath Sreedharan
arxiv-2501-17704.description: Abstract One of the significant challenges to generating value-aligned behavior is to not only account for the specified user objectives but also any implicit or unspecified user requirements. The existence of such implicit requirements could be particularly common in settings where the user’s understanding of the task model may differ from the agent’s estimate of the model.

arxiv-2508-11729.title: The Stories We Govern By: AI, Risk, and the Power of Imaginaries
arxiv-2508-11729.creator: Ninell Oldenburg, Gleb Papyshev
arxiv-2508-11729.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ninell Oldenburg, Gleb Papyshev. This paper examines how competing sociotechnical imaginaries of artificial intelligence (AI) risk shape governance decisions and regulatory constraints. Drawing on concepts from science and technology studies, we analyse three dominant narrative groups: existential risk proponents, who emphasise catastrophic AGI scenarios; accelerationists, who portray AI as a transformative force to be unleashed; and critical AI scholars, who foreground present-day harms rooted in systemic inequality.

arxiv-2510-01929.title: Inverse Language Modeling towards Robust and Grounded LLMs
arxiv-2510-01929.creator: Davide Gabrielli, Simone Sestito, Iacopo Masi
arxiv-2510-01929.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Davide Gabrielli, Simone Sestito, Iacopo Masi. The current landscape of defensive mechanisms for LLMs is fragmented and underdeveloped, unlike prior work on classifiers. To further promote adversarial robustness in LLMs, we propose Inverse Language Modeling (ILM), a unified framework that simultaneously 1) improves the robustness of LLMs to input perturbations, and, at the same time, 2) enables native grounding by inverting model outputs to identify potentially toxic or unsafe input triggers.

They naturally divide themselves into researches on sound, light and electricity, but extend into other branches of physics as well.

pmc-10686959.title: Prevalence of Comorbid Factors in Patients With Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection in ECOSPOR III, a Randomized Trial of an Oral Microbiota–Based Therapeutic
pmc-10686959.creator: Charles S Berenson, Bret Lashner, Louis Y Korman, Elizabeth Hohmann, Abhishek Deshpande, Thomas J Louie, Matthew Sims, Darrell Pardi, Colleen S Kraft, Elaine E L Wang, Stuart H Cohen, Paul Feuerstadt, Caterina Oneto, Bharat Misra, John Pullman, Ananya De, Asli Memisoglu, David A Lombardi, Brooke R H
pmc-10686959.description: BackgroundAlthough comorbidities are risk factors for recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI), many clinical trials exclude patients with medical conditions such as malignancy or immunosuppression. In a phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial (ECOSPOR III), fecal microbiota spores, live (VOWST, Seres Therapeutics; hereafter “VOS,” formerly SER-109), an oral microbiota therapeutic, significantly reduced the risk of rCDI at week 8.

pmc-11377346.title: Gan-jiang-ling-zhu decoction improves steatohepatitis by regulating gut microbiota-mediated 12-tridecenoic acid inhibition
pmc-11377346.creator: Ruohui Xu, Jiaxuan Wu, Jiashu Pan, Shengan Zhang, Yunuo Yang, Li Zhang, Wenjun Zhou, Na Wu, Dan Hu, Guang Ji, Yanqi Dang
pmc-11377346.description: Introduction: Gan–jiang–ling–zhu (GJLZ) decoction is a classical traditional Chinese medicine prescription. Through invigorating yang, activating qi and dissipating dampness, GJLZ decoction is widely applied for the treatment of chronic digestive disease, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. However, efficacy and mechanism of GJLZ decoction behind nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) treatment remains unelucidated.

pmc-12508055.description: The growing body of research on cardiac epitranscriptomic factors has underscored their potential biological roles and impact on heart development and disease. pmc-13297842.creator: Süleyman Özen, Muzaffer Sancı
pmc-13297842.description: Background/Objectives: Preoperative differentiation of benign, borderline, and malignant ovarian tumors remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic significance of PIV in ovarian tumors.

pmc-13550958.title: Revealing Functional Traits of Insect Pest Suppressive Rhizobacterial Strains Through Comparative Genomics
pmc-13550958.creator: Edward C Cairns, Francesco Del Carratore, James P J Hall, Sharon E Zytynska
pmc-13550958.description: Root inoculation with rhizobacteria is an emerging strategy to enhance plant resistance to aphid herbivory, yet the microbial functional traits underpinning these responses remain poorly characterised. Here, we present a comparative genomic analysis of five rhizobacteria ( Acidovorax radicis N35, Bacillus subtilis B171, Bacillus velezensis FZB42, Rhizobium radiobacter F4 and Pseudomonas simiae WCS417r) that suppress aphids when inoculated onto barley.

pmc-13568324.title: Climate-Impact Uncertainty in Bio-Asphalt–Rubber Binders: Probabilistic Cradle-to-Gate Screening of Bio-Oil Inventory and Crumb Rubber Allocation
pmc-13568324.creator: Yemao Zhang, Xijuan Zhao
pmc-13568324.description: Bio-asphalt–rubber (BAR) binders combine plant-based bio-oil, end-of-life tire crumb rubber, and petroleum asphalt binder, but their climate advantage remains uncertain because bio-oil supply chains, asphalt-binder inventories, and tire-rubber allocation choices can substantially change cradle-to-gate results. This study develops a probabilistic cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment for one metric ton of binder at plant gate.
